lineup:B:4431459:w5.title: Mostly right, with one tight end regret
lineup:B:4431459:w5.text: Your lineup calls have been among the better ones in this league, so the fix here is small. The week that stings is Week 5, when Harold Fannin got the tight end slot and Tyler Warren went off on your bench. You owned both tight ends and still picked wrong, which is the purest form of this game.

pos:RB1:WR8.title: Running back carries this team
pos:RB1:WR8.text: Your running back points lead the league and your receiver points rank last, so every spare move should go to the receiver room. Your backs have been covering for a receiver corps in dead last, and at nine and one nobody has made you pay for it yet. That bill usually arrives in the playoffs.

proj:over:3915511:4870795.title: Your starters keep beating the projections
proj:over:3915511:4870795.text: Nothing to change here, because this is the good kind of surprise. Joe Burrow has been outscoring his projection all season while Makai Lemon keeps landing under his, so keep starting the quarterback and keep expectations modest on the rookie. The model has been wrong in your favor all year.

lineup:C:4036378:w9.title: Two quarterbacks, one slot
lineup:C:4036378:w9.text: Start here: the best available lineup has outscored the one you started by a wide margin this season. Week 9 is the case in point, when Josh Allen started at quarterback and Jordan Love outscored him from your bench. Owning two good quarterbacks means being wrong about one of them every week.

pos:DST1:FLEX8.title: Best defense in the league, worst flex
pos:DST1:FLEX8.text: Your defense points rank first and your flex points, the wild-card slot that takes a runner or a receiver, rank last, so that is the slot where attention pays. You have the bodies for it on your bench; the trouble has been choosing among them week to week. No defense in this league is good enough to carry an empty flex.

proj:under:-16034:4429160.title: The forecasts have run ahead of the results
proj:under:-16034:4429160.text: Your starters have landed under their projections on the season. The Texans defense has quietly beaten its number while De'Von Achane has missed his by the widest margin on your roster. Your defense is the only thing here outperforming its own hype.

lineup:B:3916148:w7.title: Mostly sound, one Week 7 exception
lineup:B:3916148:w7.text: Your lineup calls have been among the better ones here, so this is a narrow complaint. Week 7 is it, when Derrick Henry started at running back and had a quiet afternoon while Tony Pollard went off on your bench. Pollard has since taken a starting slot and kept it, so that regret has already paid you back.

pos:WR2:RB8.title: Second-best receivers, last-place backs
pos:WR2:RB8.text: Your receiver points rank second in the league and your running back points rank last, which is the whole story of this roster. You carry six running backs, so the answer is not another body but one of them turning into a starter. Tony Pollard has been making the best case for the job.

proj:under:4239993:4870808.title: Slightly under forecast, and fixable
proj:under:4239993:4870808.text: Your starters have come in a little short of projection this season, and both ends of it sit close together. Tee Higgins has been beating his number while Jeremiyah Love has been missing his. Higgins is already in your lineup, which is the right call, and Love is on injured reserve, which settles the other half.
